avoid: Homer Banks, who wrote the Staple Singers' ‘If You're Ready (Come Go with Me)’, also wrote ‘A Lot of Love’, whose music formed the basis of the Spencer Davis Group's ‘Gimme Some Lovin'’.
For a Muscle Shoals session with The Staple Singers, Stax songwriter Carl Hampton shipped his piano to his hotel to pair as many songs as possible.
The Staple Singers' ‘If You're Ready (Come Go with Me)’ was a single conspicuously crafted as a spiritual successor to the group's previous chart-topper, ‘I'll Take You There’.
When Al Bell first brought them to the Swampers' Alabama studio in 1970, the family was surprised to discover that the band behind the Muscle Shoals soul hits was white.
In October 1974 Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples sent a telegram to Al Bell asking to cancel the group's contract, and Bell took it personally and fired off a blistering reply.
Terry Manning, who worked at Stax, said he co-produced the group with Al Bell, staying after Bell left at night to add orchestration parts and other overdubs.
At the age of eight, Mavis Staples was already a standout; she later recalled people coming up crying and putting money in her hand without her understanding why.
